questions.question: Explain what is meant by the generous acceptance of strangers in farming societies.
questions.expected_answer: In many African farming societies, it was a strong custom to give a visitor or stranger food and shelter. A stranger who asked to stay could be accepted into the community, given land to use and protected by the chief, as long as they respected the chief and the customs. This helped Khoisan people and farmers to live together.

questions.question: Describe three ways the first farmers and the Khoisan interacted.
questions.expected_answer: They traded: San hunters offered skins, ivory, beads, honey and meat, and farmers offered grain, pots and iron tools. Some San worked for farmers as hunters or herders. San rainmakers were asked to help in droughts. People married each other, and many Khoisan were integrated into farming communities.

questions.question: What evidence shows that Khoisan people were integrated into farming societies?
questions.expected_answer: isiXhosa and isiZulu have click sounds and some words that came from Khoisan languages; scientists have found that many South Africans have Khoisan as well as farming ancestors; and archaeologists have found farmers' pottery at San sites and San tools at farming villages.
